time.desc: A short video platform and the government have their first oral argument at the federal appeals court over the "stripping or banning" law, with the two sides clashing over freedom of speech and national security risks.
Multiple states and regions filed a joint lawsuit against the short video platform on the grounds of "addictive design to harm minors". The platform publicly denied the main accusation.

Due to blackening defects in litigation materials, the content of internal documents was restored by media technology and it was revealed that the platform had formulated lobbying plans to influence policy figures. The relevant materials were subsequently applied for sealing.

The government of an allied country ordered the closure of the local company's operations of the short video platform based on the conclusion of the national security review (without prohibiting people from continuing to use the app), and the platform stated that it would file a judicial challenge
The Federal Court of Appeal ruled to uphold the legal arrangement of “forced divestment or ban” and clarified the sales cutoff. The platform announced that it will appeal to the Supreme Court.
The short video platform submitted an emergency application to the Supreme Court requesting to suspend the implementation of the ban before the final hearing.
The Supreme Court decided to expedite the platform’s appeal against the “strive or ban” law and set a date for oral arguments, but did not immediately issue a temporary injunction.
National leader-elect files papers with Supreme Court requesting extension of divestment/debarment cutoff to give new government time to negotiate

The government filed papers with the Supreme Court opposing the request to delay enforcement and asking for its dismissal, while the platforms filed additional legal papers continuing to argue that the law infringes on free speech
Country A The Minister of Transport opened the Platform X account before the party conference, and the first video reached one million views within hours
Platform X announced the closure of its music streaming products, shrinking the front line and focusing on responding to the regulatory crisis

Platform X For the first time, a spokesperson issued a statement on the accidental leak of internal documents, denying the accusation that the algorithm was knowingly harmful to children and addictive in a short period of time.
The Minister of Innovation of an allied country issued a statement formally ordering Platform X to close local business operations due to the conclusion of the national security review.
Internet law experts publicly pointed out that shutting down companies rather than restricting applications may weaken accountability but cannot eliminate security risks.
The governor of a certain region settled in Platform X, started his campaign with a "Dad Joke" video and quickly accumulated millions of fans

The attorney general of a southern agricultural state successfully requested the court to seal the entire complaint and no longer disclose it to the public after internal documents related to the lawsuit were restored and disclosed by media technology.
